convoLines.text: «Hei... unasema Kiswahili? Hapana? ...lahaula.»
«Hasa hivyo. Kama ulivyosema.» They nod back, slowly. "Hello?"
«Wewe ni mtu mwema.» (you catch 'mwema' — good) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Sitaisahau wema huu.» (you catch 'wema' — kindness) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Wewe ndiye... kiongozi hapa?» (you catch 'kiongozi' — leader)
Wanjiru laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — Sahihi.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about? That's the whole of it."
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
"Still on what you're good at."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
«Vizuri uwepo hapa. Kweli.» (you catch 'Vizuri' — good)
«Ndiyo, uko sahihi.» (Yes, you're correct. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«Kila kitu kitakuwa sawa.» (Everything will be okay. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Okay?"
«Asante kwa kuwa hapa.» (Thanks for being here. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Huku watu hulala wapi? Ni salama?» (Here where do people sleep? Is it safe? — you're fairly sure)
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you're better with your hands than people expect. I've been waiting to see."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Lena shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us? Don't look away from this."
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Still on what you think happened to us, as it were."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took Wanjiru and Petra — Windfall, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
«Habari! Wewe... jina lako nani?» (Hello! You... what is your name? — you're fairly sure)
«Ndiyo, ndiyo, hasa.» (Yes, yes, exactly. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«Wewe ni mtu mwema.» (You are a good person. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Okay?"
«Sitaisahau wema huu.» (I will not forget this kindness. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Una chakula? Chochote?» (Do you have food? Anything? — you're fairly sure)
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"Still on what you did for fun."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "The whole fire was arguing about Static last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Big' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know where the wild ramps grows thick — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Static? Willow is pushing 'Big Big'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d6: 🕯️ Simone Vargas is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d8: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Flashbulb Moth is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d7: That night, they bring Simone home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d7: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d8: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d8: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d8: ◈ SYSTEM: "RATINGS DIP. The audience wants STAKES — pointed ones. A PALISADE. Stockpile 14,000 kcal, 350 wood and 60 stone. Walls make such good television. You will thank us when the teeth come."
d8: SYSTEM: Neural interface stable. Text overlay enabled.
d8: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 20. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 2."

d8: ◈ THE SPARK — something clicks. A trick Siobhan learned long ago suddenly has edges it never had. SYSTEM: "ANOMALY: organic unit demonstrates pattern recognition. Slot capacity increased. We are taking notes." (Ability slots: 2)
d8: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d8: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d8: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
burialWindowSay: d6: 📖 LEARNED: Grave Robber (Level 1). You can loot the dead (villagers, monsters). Good gear. -15 trust if seen.
d7: That night, they bring Simone home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d7: 📻 "Why do the small humans keep putting organic matter in their FACE-HOLES? We built you a fusion pellet! ...You BURIED it. WHY did you bury the pellet?!"
d9: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+6 integration)
d10: You say a few words for them. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d10: You bury them. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+2 trauma)
echoV2Sample: d10: The village raises a marker by the fire — Simone, day 10. a hushwolf. A place to stand.
echoV2DeltaSample: d10: The village raises a marker by the fire — Simone, day 10. a hushwolf. A place to stand.

lastSay: d50: — DAY 50 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d50: Overnight, Blackberry went bad — beyond saving. You leave it for the flies.
d50: Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.
d50: 💬 Wanjiru says: "They said you're doing well. It sounded... proud? Can they feel proud?"
d50: You wake with a start — something is wrong.
